newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia to deport former U.S. Black Panther.
newsitem.headline: Australia to deport former U.S. Black Panther.

text.p: Australia on Tuesday ordered the deportation of a former U.S. Black Panther activist, once convicted of hijacking an aircraft.
Acting Immigration Minister Amanda Vanstone said black human rights activist Lorenzo Ervin's visa had been cancelled and he was being detained pending his deportation.
"The government is concerned that the integrity of Australia's entry systems are not undermined by the entry or stay of people who are not of good character," Vanstone said in a statement.
"As Mr Ervin was now an unlawful non-citizen he had been detained by immigration while arrangements were made for his departure," Vanstone said.

Ervin, who was invited to Australia for a four-week speaking tour by anarchist group Angry People, was convicted in the United States in 1969 of hijacking a plane to Cuba. He was given two life sentences, but released from jail in 1983.
Prime Minister John Howard on Monday said Ervin, who arrived on July 4, should never have been allowed into Australia.
Howard said Ervin had apparently misrepresented his past when he applied for a visa to visit Australia and had used a different surname.

Before being detained, Ervin told reporters in Brisbane that he had not falsified his immigration documents and that the Australian government was attempting to stifle freedom of speech. "We maintain this is a free speech case and nothing more," Ervin said.
